issues.description: The script sends user location data (latitude, longitude, formatted address) to discord.com via a webhook, which is a third-party server. This is triggered by user action or feature toggles.
issues.recommendation: Warn users about the privacy risk and allow disabling this feature. Ensure webhook URLs are not hardcoded or shared.

issues.description: The script sends user coordinates to nominatim.openstreetmap.org to retrieve address information. While this is a public geocoding API, it transmits user location data externally.
issues.recommendation: Inform users that their location data is sent to a third-party geocoding service.

issues.description: The script reads coordinates from the page, including from React fiber nodes and iframe properties, which may include sensitive location data.
issues.recommendation: Limit data collection to only what is necessary for the script's functionality.

issues.description: The script requests notification permission and uses the Notification API to send notifications.
issues.recommendation: Ensure notifications are not abused and only used for legitimate purposes.

issues.description: The script grants GM_xmlhttpRequest, which is used for external requests, and GM_setValue/GM_getValue for persistent storage. All granted permissions are used.
issues.recommendation: No excessive permissions detected, but review GM_xmlhttpRequest usage for scope.

issues.description: The script modifies Element.prototype.setAttribute to ignore sandbox attribute for iframes, which may weaken frame protection.
issues.recommendation: Do not bypass sandboxing unless absolutely necessary. This may expose the page to clickjacking or iframe-based attacks.

details: Reads coordinates from page elements and React fiber nodes
Sends location data to external APIs

script_name: CheatGuessr Universal (Works in GeoGuessr | OpenGuessr | WorldGuessr | FreeGuessr)
summary: This script transmits user location data to third-party servers (discord.com and nominatim.openstreetmap.org), collects sensitive location information from the page, and modifies iframe sandboxing. These behaviors pose critical privacy and data exfiltration risks. No code obfuscation or DOM XSS detected. Supply chain risk is low as no @require is used. The script is not safe for privacy-sensitive users.
